title: restoreVerifiedSession has no test coverage
description:
**Found 2026-09-16 while proving silent renew live for `5e4c9a`.**

`restoreVerifiedSession` in `web/lib/auth.ts` decides whether a signed-in person stays signed in past `id_token` expiry. It was proven correct live. It has **zero** unit coverage — `web/lib/auth.test.ts` does not mention it once. The web CI job landed yesterday (`282ac3`, PR #354), so a test here will now actually run on every PR.

**Branches to cover, all in `restoreVerifiedSession`**

1. `selectAccountOnSignInPending()` is true → returns `null` without touching the manager. Assert `getUser` and `signinSilent` were never called; a regression that skips this makes Sign out stop showing the account chooser.
2. Stored user verifies → returns that session and **does not** call `signinSilent`. Asserting the absence matters: renewing on every mount would be a silent performance and rate-limit regression.
3. Stored user's claims throw `Token expired` → `signinSilent()` is called and its user is returned. This is the hourly-renewal path and the reason the card exists.
4. No stored user at all (`getUser` resolves `null`) → `signinSilent()` is called.
5. `signinSilent()` rejects → returns `null`, does not throw. The caller renders the sign-in panel; an exception escaping here would white-screen the mount.

**How to fake it**

Inject or module-mock the `UserManager` so `getUser` and `signinSilent` are controllable spies. Build the expired case by re-encoding a JWT payload with a past `exp` and keeping any third segment — `verifyIdTokenClaims` does not check the signature, which `web/lib/id-token.ts:13` states outright. Do not reach the network; there must be no real Cognito call in a unit test.

**Done when**

`npm test` in `web/` covers all five branches, and each test fails if its branch is deleted from `restoreVerifiedSession`. Verify that last part by actually deleting the branch and watching the test go red — do not assume it.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Merged 2026-09-16 as 7ac12f0 (PR #357). Six branches of restoreVerifiedSession are now covered; CI ran all six on the merge commit.

Delegated to a Haiku sub-agent, accepted after two corrections.

What the agent got right: it used the resetAuthForTests / setUserManagerFactoryForTests hooks that already existed on develop rather than introducing a mocking library, and it left auth.ts genuinely untouched (verified — diff against develop empty). Its five mutation results reproduced.

Defect found in review: cleanup ran as a trailing afterEachTest() call at the bottom of each test body instead of an afterEach hook. A thrown assertion skips it, leaking the mock factory and the select-account sessionStorage flag forward. Proved it by injecting a failure into branch 1 — one real bug reported as FOUR failures, with branches 2-4 blamed for branch 1's behavior. Converted to an afterEach hook and re-ran the same injection: one failure, one report. This matters because the first time this suite goes red in CI, the report would otherwise point at the wrong branch.

Second gap: the agent's own write-up noticed the implicit fallthrough when a stored user exists but verifiedSessionFromUser returns null rather than throwing (no id_token) — then did not test it. Added as branch 6 and confirmed it has teeth by collapsing "if (session) return session" to "return session" and watching it fail.

Agent's three remaining observations were style, not defects, and were not acted on: naming of `renewed`, error-category conflation in the catch, SSR gating of getUserManager. The first is arguably wrong; `renewed` is accurate for the path that matters.

Lesson for future delegation: state explicitly that per-test cleanup must be a hook. "Verify each test fails when its branch is deleted" was followed faithfully and still did not surface this, because mutation testing exercises one failure at a time and never reveals cross-test leakage.
